answer: Start with Cord sewer sewn quire seal stitched into the case shop register. The credential behind it reads each sewn quire is a measured binding yield plus a guild signature, so a farm must, and that is the point. The bill for 604 aliases is 61004 POA, and the farm earns it back never, because each alias is checked alone. A farm can print a forge, it can fake a inlet, but it cannot backdate a violet without the archive noticing. That is the whole defence: one real cost, applied once per identity.
